scalars.scalar_value: A Juris Doctor (J.D.) degree and estate planning experience are required, or equivalent combination of education and experience including professional designations such as Certified Financial Planner (CFP), Certified Public Accountant (CPA), or Certified Specialist in Planned Giving (CSPG).

The regular hours for this full-time position are 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., Monday – Friday, except during the designated summer period when office hours end at 4:30 p.m. Overtime, holiday, weekend and evening work hours may be required. Regular hours may vary due to needs of the College or division.

items.item_text: A Juris Doctor (J.D.) degree and estate planning experience are required, or equivalent combination of education and experience including professional designations such as Certified Financial Planner (CFP), Certified Public Accountant (CPA), or Certified Specialist in Planned Giving (CSPG).

The ideal candidate will have a minimum of seven years of professional work with clients or donors in the areas of estate or legacy planning. Management experience is required. Experience in an academic setting is strongly preferred, as is working in a fundraising campaign environment. Required Knowledge and Critical Skills This individual must possess the knowledge, skills, and ability to successfully perform the essential functions of the job or must be able to demonstrate how the essential functions will be performed through knowledge, skills, and abilities not listed below. • Understand and communicate the mission and history of the College’s liberal arts environment. • Thorough knowledge of various gift planning options including bequests, trusts, outright gifts; various types of gifts including securities, insurance, collectibles, real estate and other financial vehicles; charitable giving tax laws; and methods and means of planned giving. • An understanding of basic investment concepts [in addition to familiarity with charitable trust accounting.] • Have experience in tax, estate, and financial planning and in dealing with and advising donors and prospects. • Remain current on tax laws and be willing to learn every day as donors present new issues to be resolved. • Experience working in a comprehensive capital campaign, preferably in a higher education setting. • A proven track record of success in personally identifying, qualifying, cultivating, soliciting, and stewarding gifts of complex assets and/or complex giving vehicles from individuals. • Comfort and effectiveness in working with high-net-worth individuals; experience in international settings a plus. • Demonstrated effectiveness and clarity of verbal and written communication with excellent interpersonal communication skills, cultural competency, and ability to work with, facilitate, motivate and inspire a diverse group of donors, prospects, colleagues, volunteers, and constituents. • Must handle all activities with discretion, tact, and a keen eye for detail. • Working knowledge of basic math and statistics. • Proficient use of Microsoft Office Suite (such as Word, Excel, Outlook); experience utilizing customer relationship management software (such as Salesforce) is preferred. • Able to meet multiple deadlines and work both independently and as a collaborative member of Advancement and the College in support of the College’s strategic vision and the division’s annual goals, with a high standard of integrity and ethics.

Design, build, and lead the growth and development of a complex assets and legacy giving program, including a robust pipeline of significant legacy gifts that align with Pomona College’s long-term fundraising strategy and achievement of annual and multi-year comprehensive campaign goals.

Maintain a personal portfolio of high-capacity donors and prospects with potential for complex assets and major legacy gifts, and demonstrate frontline fundraising success through identification, cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship.
Serve as the College’s recognized expert in gifts of complex assets, as well as bequests, trusts and other deferred giving.
Collaborate with senior leadership as well as donors and their financial, tax, and estate advisors to develop and present complex gift strategies tailored to their particular circumstances.
Lead in the creation, design and execution of Pomona College’s complex asset strategies and goals and develop metrics to measure ongoing success and ROI.
Achieve personal annual fundraising goals with a focus on legacy giving from alumni, families, donors, and prospects.
Recruit and supervise one complex assets and legacy giving coordinator or assistant director. Develop a comprehensive, metrics-based, fundraising plan and set aspirational goals.
Operationalize short and long-term complex assets goals and strategies, with an emphasis on legacy giving, to build upon existing commitments and expand the current donor base of support.

Provide training to frontline fundraisers relating to gifts of complex assets and legacy giving, implementing a breadth of tools, such as short instructional videos, in-person coaching workshops, and 1:1 case strategy reviews.

Collaborate with and support major gift, life-income gift (Pomona Plan), reunion and family giving fundraisers in cultivating complex assets and legacy gifts from alumni, families, donors, and prospects that may combine major outright, life-income, complex assets and legacy gifts into their annual planning and strategy sessions.
Develop and implement strategies to maximize the acquisition and retention of alumni, families, donors and others as complex asset and legacy giving prospects.

Develop and coordinate a comprehensive multi-channel marketing plan, materials and program activities that promote and support complex assets and legacy giving, in strategic partnership with the Office of Advancement Communications.

Lead the transformation of the College’s legacy giving society, the Granite & Sagebrush Society, to become a group that is inspired, informed, and engaged. In collaboration with the stewardship and events teams, help develop a strategic plan for effective and impactful stewardship of alumni, families, legacy giving donors and prospects, with the goal of significantly increasing membership in the Granite & Sagebrush Society.
Introduce and implement a roster of virtual and in-person events, as well as other carefully considered stewardship and cultivation moves.

Working closely with outside trust and estate counsel, executors, trustees, and other estate administrators, oversee the tracking and receipt of matured estate expectancies to ensure the preservation and timely distribution of all estate gifts to Pomona College.
Build and nurture strong relationships with financial, legal and tax advisors in support of complex assets and legacy giving to Pomona College.
Serve as an expert on and assist in the drafting and review of simple and complex donor gift agreements and statements of intention.

Lead the development and implementation of legacy giving counting policy and develop and implement strategies to improve realized estate gift forecasting in partnership with Advancement Services and the Office of the Vice President for Advancement.
Foster a leadership style that inspires, empowers, and motivates staff while promoting a collaborative and inclusive work environment.

Partner, coach, equip and encourage development staff to pursue complex assets gift opportunities, assisting them in the design and implementation of individualized strategies for the identification, qualification, cultivation, solicitation and stewardship of planned, major and blended gifts as appropriate.
Perform other duties as requested, delegated, or assigned.
